html:
The Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates were the first Islamic states after the death of Muhammad, ruling from 632 to 750. Within a century they reached from Spain to the Indus, one of the fastest expansions in history.

The Rashidun, 632 to 661. The first four caliphs, "the rightly guided", were close companions of the Prophet and ruled from Medina.

  • Abu Bakr held Arabia together after Muhammad's death.
  • Umar led the great conquests: Syria after the Battle of the Yarmuk in 636, Iraq, Egypt and most of Iran.
  • Uthman issued the standard text of the Quran but was murdered in 656.
  • Ali, Muhammad's cousin, ruled through the first Muslim civil war and was murdered in 661.

The Umayyads, 661 to 750. Muawiya, governor of Syria, took power and founded a dynasty ruling from Damascus. Making the caliphate hereditary angered many, and his son's forces killed Ali's son Husayn at Karbala in 680.

The Umayyads built a working empire. Abd al-Malik built the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, made Arabic the language of government and struck the gold dinar. Under al-Walid I armies took North Africa, invaded Spain in 711 and reached Sindh and Central Asia. Attempts to take Constantinople failed.

Non-Arab Muslims resented being treated as second class, and Ali's supporters never accepted the dynasty. In 750 a revolt from Khorasan overthrew the Umayyads and founded the Abbasid Caliphate. One Umayyad prince escaped to Spain, where his line ruled from Córdoba.
sum: The Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates were the first Islamic states after the death of Muhammad, ruling from 632 to 750. Within a century they reached from Spain to the Indus, one of the fastest expansions in history.
